summary: Andrey Terentyev is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University (~1970–1975) and held a post at the Museum of the History of Religion.

Andrzej Gawroński was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv (1902–1906) and the University of Leipzig (~1903–1906). He taught Indo-European linguistics at Jagiellonian University (1916–1917) and contrastive linguistics at the University of Lviv (1917).

András Róna-Tas is a linguist and scholar of Tibetology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences under Gyula Ortutay and Lajos Ligeti, later serving as professor at the University of Szeged (1968–2002).

André Bareau was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Sorbonne, EPHE, and Collège de France under Jean Filliozat and Paul Demiéville, later serving as directeur d'études at EPHE (1956–1973) and directeur at Collège de France (1971–1991).

André Caquot was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and École Pratique des Hautes Études, later holding posts at EPHE (~1955–1972), the University of Strasbourg, the University of Paris, and Collège de France (1972–1994).

André Couture is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He studied at Laval University (~1964–1970), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1972–1977), and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1972–1977), later holding a post at Laval University (~1978).

André Godard was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts (~1904–1909) and held a post at the University of Tehran (~1934–1953).

André Leroi-Gourhan was an archaeologist and historian. He studied at the University of Paris (~1931–1944) under Marcel Mauss and held posts at the Musée Guimet (1940–1943), the University of Paris (~1956–1969), and the Collège de France (1969–1982).

André Martinet was a linguist who studied at the Sorbonne and Humboldt University of Berlin under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1938–1946), Columbia University (~1947–1955), and the University of Paris (~1955–1978).
André Mazon was a linguist. He studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1900–1904) and Charles University (~1903–1904), and he held a post at the Collège de France from 1923 to 1951.

André Padoux was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Louis Renou, Olivier Lacombe, and Lakshman Joo, among others. He served as director at the Institut Français d'Histoire en Allemagne and Directeur de Recherche at the CNRS.
André Wedemeyer was a scholar of Sinology and Japanology who completed his doctoral studies under August Conrady (~1910–1916). He held a post at the University of Leipzig.

André-Georges Haudricourt was a linguist and sinologist who studied under Marcel Mauss. He held posts at the Muséum national d'histoire naturelle, CNRS (~1940–1976), École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1948–1949), and Paris Descartes University (~1970–1976).

Angela Falco Howard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and art history/archaeology. She completed her doctoral dissertation at New York University under Alexander Coburn Soper and served as a professor at Rutgers University (attested 2005).
Angela Manderscheid is a scholar of Tibetology. She has held posts at Freie Universität Berlin and at the University of Oulu as a researcher (attested 1998).

Angela Sumegi is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa under Nalini Devdas and held an assistant professorship at Carleton University (attested 2008).

Angela Zito is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1980–1989) and became an associate professor of anthropology and religious studies at New York University (~1999).

Angelika Krebs is a philosopher who studied at Freiburg, Konstanz, UC Berkeley, New College, and Goethe University Frankfurt under Bernard Williams. She held posts at Konstanz, Frankfurt (1993–2001), and the Chair of Practical Philosophy at the University of Basel (2001).

Angelika Malinar is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz and the University of Tübingen. She held teaching posts at Freie Universität Berlin and SOAS, becoming extraordinary professor of Indology at the University of Zurich (2009).

Angelo De Gubernatis was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Turin and Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Florence (1863–1891) and Rome (1890).
